content.title: Investigate bunx playwright test loader failure
content.description:
During validation of the backend isolation fix (mqe074zvth), I observed that 'bunx playwright test' became unable to load test files after a lockfile re-save event. Symptoms: repeated 'Error: Only URLs with a scheme in file, data, and node are supported by the default ESM loader. Received protocol bun:' messages on stderr, followed by 'Error: Playwright Test did not expect test.describe to be called here' and 'Error: No tests found'. The suite exited with code 0 despite finding no tests.

Switching to 'npx playwright test' resolved it immediately and produced 152/152 passing. Both webServers (bun run dev:server and cd frontend and bun run dev) start fine when invoked manually, so the issue is specific to how bunx resolves the playwright test loader after a lockfile re-save.

This is NOT related to the isolation fix (which is validated and working). It is a bun tooling or module-resolution concern. Filing as an idea because: (a) the team's documented run command is bunx playwright test, (b) if this is reproducible it undermines the determinism guarantee of the isolation fix, (c) it may be worth standardizing the e2e runner invocation (npx vs bunx) or adding a note to the README.

Reproduction context: observed after roughly 30 bunx playwright invocations during validation. A 'Saved lockfile' message preceded the failure. bun install reports no changes, so the lockfile content is stable — the re-save itself seems to perturb bunx's resolution.
